phases.name: 1. Recon — find every service
phases.goal: Full port sweep, then enumerate each service deeply. Map every open port to a plan.
steps: exact nmap passes + the port->service->plan table

phases.name: 2. Service — attack what's open
phases.goal: Pick the plan for each open port; test every input until something gives a way in.
steps: oscp cmd web   ·   oscp cmd smb   ·   oscp cmd services

phases.name: 3. Foothold — turn the bug into a shell
phases.goal: Start a listener, fire a reverse shell in the target's language, and catch it.
steps: pick a reverse shell (LHOST filled in)
oscp hacktools php   ·   oscp hacktools windows   ·   oscp hacktools msfvenom

phases.name: 4. Stabilise — get a real TTY
phases.goal: Upgrade the dumb shell so you have job control, history and arrow keys.
steps: the python-pty + stty raw upgrade, step by step
oscp atlas rlwrap   ·   oscp atlas pwncat-cs

phases.name: 5. Enumerate — local recon as the new user
phases.goal: Grab the first flag, run the enumerator, hunt and reuse credentials.
steps: the first 10 minutes on a box
oscp atlas linpeas   ·   oscp atlas winpeas
find creds, then reuse them everywhere

phases.name: 6. Escalate — root / SYSTEM
phases.goal: Map each enumeration finding to the technique that escalates it.
steps: sudo / suid / capability abuse by binary
oscp cmd privesc-linux   ·   oscp cmd privesc-windows   ·   oscp cmd ad

phases.name: 7. Loot & proof — capture and pivot
phases.goal: Prove each flag properly, loot credentials, and pivot to any further hosts.
steps: dump and crack what you find
reach deeper hosts (chisel / ligolo / ssh tunnels)

phases.name: 8. Report — the write-up that scores
phases.goal: A reproducible per-machine report. Points come from the report, not the shell.
steps: structure + what each machine section needs
how to take notes as you go
